sample_unit: clinical interview transcripts (older adults referred for neuropsychological evaluation)
models_evaluated: 10 commercially available general-purpose LLMs (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic classification agreement with clinician reference diagnoses on interview transcripts
links.effect: Exact agreement 18.8% to 56.2%; Cohen's kappa -.178 to .196; tendency to overclassify impairment; specificity 0 to 60% despite sensitivity over 90% in seven of ten models.
links.quote: Model-inferred and reference diagnoses showed exact agreement rates from 18.8% to 56.2% with poor to slight chance-corrected agreement (Cohen’s κ = −.178 to .196).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of 10 commercial LLMs for diagnostic classification of cognitive impairment from unstructured clinical interview transcripts, benchmarking accuracy/agreement against clinical reference diagnoses.
